#1762. GdS: Tactics, data and team-mates – the ‘strange case’ of Goncalo Ramos at Milan

The Goncalo Ramos enigma continues to dominate the newspaper columns, as AC Milan try unlock their record signing.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport report, Milan fans hoped they had finally found a top-class striker in Ramos, but his three goals this season are not sufficient compared to expectations and the €70m price tag for which he arrived.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

And yet, the Portuguese centre-forward is still proving to be a factor in the team’s fortunes. The reason for this lies behind statistics that the average fan might ignore, but Ruben Amorim certainly isn’t.

The coach has repeatedly emphasised how Ramos is helping the team, less so the other way around. Looking at the numbers, you can’t argue with him. Gonçalo may not be making it into the top scorers’ table, but his work is well explained by statistics that place him among the top strikers in Serie A.

Which ones? Passes (20.7 per game, first in volume among centre-forwards in the league ahead of Lazio’s Noslin) or touches (2nd), for example. But also the aerial duels won and fouls drawn (19, first among attackers) underscore the importance of his sacrifice too.

There are two considerations that don’t emerge from the statistics, but are equally important. The first concerns the movements that free up or facilitate team-mates, such as the sprint for Milan’s first goal in Genoa.

Alphadjo Cisse found himself all alone in the penalty area thanks to Ramos drawing two of the Rossoblu central defenders towards him, allowing Adrien Rabiot to easily pass to the young Italian who was in lots of space.

The second consideration concerns the pressure and coverage work, which has changed since the start of the season. In the early days, Gonçalo was the first to apply pressure up front, but in doing so, he exposed Modric to too much space to cover in front of or behind him.

Amorim therefore asked the Portuguese to instead harass the opposing playmaker, without attacking the defence in the initial possession. This move allows Luka to run less and think more during the opponent’s possession phase.

We were talking about a Milan side that is helping Ramos less than the centre-forward is helping the team, too. The former Benfica man is 19th in Serie A for shots (26) and 15th for shots on target (10).

While it’s true that the Rossoneri maintain a high standard in terms of the quality of chances created (third in the league for big chances behind Inter and Roma), it’s equally undeniable that they arrive in the final third of the pitch less often than expected. Milan are 12th for touches in the opponent’s penalty area and 12th for shots on target.

In short, Ramos sees the ball mostly where he can’t hurt the goalkeepers. Even if, in relation to goal-scoring chances, he should have scored double in the league: 4.16 xG compared to the just two scored. Still, not enough for a Milan-calibre player.

#1761. Koeman backs Barcelona as favourites in LaLiga and Champions League

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Former Barcelona player and head coach Ronald Koeman has backed the Blaugrana to win both LaLiga and the Champions League this season.

Barca have made a strong start in both competitions this term, with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid before the international break seeing Hansi Flick's side sit top of LaLiga.

They have won their first six away games in a league campaign for just the third time, after 2010-11 and 2012-13, while also winning 11 of their 12 games overall (L1) in LaLiga.

Indeed, Barca have only lost two matches in 2026-27, going down to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League and Real Madrid in LaLiga.

The Blaugrana are fifth in the Champions League standings after four games, scoring 14 goals across those matches.

While Koeman believes winning the European competition will be harder than retaining their league title, he still sees Barca as favourites to win both competitions.

"We shouldn't get nervous about the two defeats, against PSG and Real Madrid. You can lose against PSG," Koeman said a charity event at Barcelona Golf Club.

— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) November 11, 2026

"I see Barca as strong; they have a great team and a great coach. Barca are the big favourites for La Liga; the Champions League is another story. Then, in the knockout stage, you can have a tough night. But they're still the favourites.

"Flick's Baraa takes a lot of risks, but it gives a lot to football. Their style of play gives a lot to the fans.

"There are risks with the high defensive line if there's no pressure on the ball… we saw that against Real Madrid. But they're on the right track."

Barca host Villarreal in their first match after the international break on November 22, before travelling to Azerbaijan to face Sabah in the Champions League.

#1760. Chelsea injury news: Moises Caicedo provides update that will worry Xabi Alonso

By Darren Plant | 12 Nov 2026 11:29

Chelsea midfielder Moises Caicedo has suggested that he plans to play for Ecuador with "a few problems".

Caicedo played the full 90 minutes as Chelsea suffered a 1-0 defeat to Sunderland at the Stadium of Light on Sunday afternoon.

However, the 25-year-old had been regarded as a fitness doubt prior to that game, Xabi Alonso telling reporters that one of his star players had been suffering with a minor issue.

As expected, Caicedo has linked up with the Ecuador squad for their upcoming friendlies versus Costa Rica and Bolivia.

Nevertheless, speaking to local reporters, he has given the impression that he is far from feeling 100% fit.

In comments covered by FutbolEcuador, Caicedo has revealed his intention to play through the pain barrier for his country.

He said: "I’m a little…[sighs] fine, a bit tired, having a few problems, but well, I’m here.

"Honestly, my national team is what matters most to me, being here with my people, with my Ecuador. I’m making a huge effort to be here, and I’m very happy about that."

While Alonso will have concerns over Caicedo representing Ecuador, the player will argue that he has his reasons.

He was forced to miss the last international period due to the calf injury that he suffered in August.

Meanwhile, at a time when he is the national team captain, Caicedo is yet to play under new head coach Marcelo Gallardo.

That appears to be behind his desire to attend this international camp, but the timing of Chelsea's next fixture is hardly ideal.

They play Leeds United in a 3pm kickoff on November 21. Ecuador do not play Bolivia until November 17, with Caicedo then having to take a long-haul flight and make up a time difference in preparation for the Leeds game.

#1759. Repubblica: Milan and Real Madrid watching as Napoli star McTominay stalls on contract

Scott McTominay’s Napoli future is in doubt, and a report has named AC Milan among the surprise potential suitors.

In a Napoli side that appears to have lost its way, one of the few lights leading the way remains McTominay. Despite a season that started on the wrong foot and a heart condition (now resolved), the Scot has five goals in 11 games this season across Serie A and the Champions League.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Massimiliano Allegri’s team is going through a tough time, and the former Manchester United player himself has had some tough nights. As La Repubblica (via Calciomercato.com) report, Napoli fans are beginning to worry about where things are heading.

The 29-year-old McTominay is at a turning point in his career, one which has been revitalised since his arrival at Napoli and the Scudetto won under Antonio Conte. His current contract with the Neapolitans expires in 2028, but negotiations for a renewal have stalled.

Fabrizio Romano reported that Napoli remain confident in the possibility of reaching an agreement over an extension, but the uncertainty currently surrounding the project, the bad results and doubts about the club’s future are forcing him to evaluate.

La Repubblica add that the discussions have even stalled after positive steps were taken in September. McTominay and his representatives want to better understand the Azzurri’s vision moving forward before finalising a new agreement.

Sky Switzerland journalist Sacho Tavolieri reported that the former Manchester United man’s agent has already held discussions with several English clubs. Napoli have not completely ruled out a possible sale, and the figure would be €25-30m.

His contract is currently worth €4.5m net per season. Napoli would like to extend it until 2030 with a salary increase, but they are unwilling to accept the Scotsman’s demands, who has requested around €7-8m net per season.

According to La Repubblica, at the end of the season McTominay and Napoli will sit down to discuss the terms of the new contract, once the club’s plans are clearer. Several clubs are interested though and are watching closely.

Aston Villa and Manchester United enquired in the summer. In the coming weeks, Real Madrid and AC Milan will also be keeping a close eye on the developments surrounding McTominay.

#1758. Leeds defender Jayden Bogle victim of racial abuse online after escaping red card for challenge on Tottenham's Mathys Tel

Published: 14:00 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 18:15 EST, 8 November 2026

Jayden Bogle has been racially abused online after Leeds’ Premier League win over Tottenham on Saturday.

His club have promised to push for ‘the strongest possible action’ if those responsible for the posts can be identified.

Leeds’ statement read: ‘Leeds United are appalled at the disgusting, racist social media abuse Jayden Bogle suffered following Saturday’s Premier League victory against Tottenham Hotspur.

‘Leeds United condemns this behaviour in the strongest possible terms. There is no place for racism in football or society.

‘The club will work with the Premier League and relevant authorities to identify the individuals and push for the strongest possible action to be taken against them.

‘Jayden has the full and unconditional support of the club and his team-mates, and we all stand with him at this time. Nobody should ever be subjected to racist abuse.’

Jayden Bogle has been the victim of sickening racial abuse after avoiding a red card for this challenge against Tottenham on Saturday

Leeds have promised to push for legal action to be taken against the abusers if they can be identified

Along with the racist and highly offensive messages, the posts, believed to have come from four separate accounts, featured emojis of monkeys and bananas.

Bogle was involved in a controversial incident during the Tottenham game. The 26-year-old escaped a red card when his studs made heavy contact with the ankle of Mathys Tel, forcing the Spurs player to go off injured.

After the game, Leeds boss Daniel Farke said: ‘Jayden is one of the fairest players in the country.

He is more like a butterfly than an eagle and he would not even foul a player on purpose, let alone injure them. It was never intentional and maybe this is why the VAR said it was not a red card.’

#1757. Aston Villa injury news: Unai Emery suffers blow ahead of key Sunderland match

By Darren Plant | 12 Nov 2026 11:51

Aston Villa midfielder Johan Manzambi has withdrawn from international duty with Switzerland.

The 21-year-old has quickly racked up three goals and four assists from 10 appearances since joining from Freiburg in the summer.

However, not only did Manzambi start the season with an injury, he is yet to complete 90 minutes in a Villa shirt.

Manzambi appeared to pick up an ankle issue against Manchester United last weekend having been on the receiving end of a heavy challenge from Leny Yoro.

Nevertheless, it appears that the playmaker has been suffering with a different problem.

A statement from the Switzerland camp claims that Manzambi arrived for duty with his national tram with a calf injury.

The statement read: "The midfielder arrived at the national team camp on Monday already suffering from a calf complaint.

"Despite intensive medical care and further assessment, his condition has not improved sufficiently, making it impossible for him to feature in either match."

Switzerland are due to play Slovenia and Scotland in their remaining UEFA Nations League matches on Friday and Monday respectively.

If Switzerland's medical staff feel that it was "impossible" for Manzambi to face Scotland on Monday, it puts his participation against Sunderland on November 21 firmly in doubt.

Villa will naturally have concerns over the physical condition of a player who cost close to £60m.

At the same time, there may be a sense of relief that he gets to enjoy a brief rest period after a hectic run of matches.

Since making his Villa debut on September 12, Manzambi has accumulated 889 minutes of football across 11 starts and three substitute outings for club and country.

When considering that he has little to no pre-season, that is a lot of game time, and Emery will be happy for him to spend a week or so on the sidelines to prepare for the next phase of the season.

#1756. Brazil winger Rayan makes ‘very good impression’ on Ancelotti

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Carlo Ancelotti revealed Rayan made a "very good impression" in training ahead of Brazil's friendly fixtures this month.

The Selecao face Japan on Saturday before taking on Singapore for the first time on November 17, with Ancelotti continuing his experiment with younger players.

Rayan earned a call-up to Brazil's World Cup squad in the summer, recording one assist, while he scored a stoppage-time equaliser against Australia during the last international break.

The Bournemouth winger has impressed since Neymar's reduced role and eventual retirement, but with Vinicius Junior, Raphinha and Estevao taking up the attacking roles, Rayan could start as a midfielder.

Ancelotti tested Rayan in midfield ahead of facing Japan, and the former Real Madrid boss liked what he saw.

"We did tests in training to see the players in different positions, we tested Rayan in this position, as a left midfielder," said Ancelotti.

"He did a good job, he showed that he can play there, just like Andrey [Santos] can.

"Rayan gave me, personally, a very good impression, because he is a player who has a lot of potential, strong, committed, focused on the game."

#1755. Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources. After claiming the first pole of his Formula One career, an absolutely stunning effort in his 192nd attempt – edging out Mercedes’ George Russell right at the death – Alpine’s Pierre Gasly revealed that a harmless jibe from his performance coach Ben Thorpe just before the session started had riled him up.

It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.

“Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference. “There are a few of us in the paddock who are. So we have exchanged our IDs on Chess.com and we have had a little game going on.

“I won yesterday, and another one that carried on into today,” the Frenchman added. “I was feeling confident and I was picking [taking] piece after piece. Then Ben told me: ‘You are getting George here but he is going to get you in a few minutes!’. And I thought ‘F--- off!’.”

What a way to break your duck. And what a day on which to do it. On Friday, Gasly lost his only podium of the season when the International Court of Appeal reinstated two five-second penalties he received in Monaco, dropping him from third to seventh in that race. The ruling produced fireworks when Flavio Briatore, Alpine’s executive adviser, then accused one of the judges on the ICA panel of being biased towards McLaren, one of two teams who had brought the appeal.

Another 24 hours later, the fireworks were for all the right reasons. And there was no appealing the result; the start of Russell’s final lap in Q3 was slightly compromised by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, but the Englishman could have no real complaints, losing out by 0.060secs in the end, prompting wild celebrations in the Alpine garage.

To say the result was a surprise would be an understatement. This was the Enstone team’s first pole in 17 years, since Fernando Alonso took P1 Renault at the 2009 Hungarian Grand Prix.

The warning signs were there. Alpine had been quick all weekend. But the Tifosi packing Monza’s grandstands fully expected it to be a battle between Mercedes and their beloved Ferrari for pole.

The Scuderia’s performance was underwhelming. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were only ninth and 10th quickest in Q2, the latter squeaking into Q3 by one thousandth of a second from Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto. “F--- me,” Hamilton said after dodging that bullet.

And although they improved a bit in Q3, Hamilton managing to claim P5, just behind Leclerc in P4, they never threatened the front row. In fact, they later got lucky as McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, who took P3, was later hit with a three-place grid drop post-qualifying for impeding Liam Lawson, meaning both Ferrari drivers rose one place.

It could prove significant. Hamilton, like Russell, knows this weekend represents a golden opportunity to close the gap to Kimi Antonelli in the title race. The two Britons are tied second in the championship heading into the weekend, 59 points behind the Italian. But Antonelli, who sacrificed his qualifying to help Russell, must start from the back of the grid on Sunday due to exceeding the permitted number of engines in a season.

It promises to be a fascinating race, with Antonelli fighting his way through the pack and Russell and Hamilton trying to make hay while they can. Russell sounded confident. “I think they [Alpine] have got a car that’s got some good straight-line speed, which will be nice for them in the race. But, yeah, confident I’ve got the pace to go for the win.”

Could he be underestimating Gasly again? The Frenchman, who lives locally in Milan and speaks fluent Italian, has won here before. He claimed the only victory of his F1 career at Monza for AlphaTauri in 2020.

“Anything is possible tomorrow,” insisted Steve Nielsen, Alpine’s managing director. “We didn’t expect to be in pole position, we are. Tomorrow, good starts, good strategy, good pit stops – who knows? Let’s try to win it.”

Gasly himself said he had no idea what he was capable of. “My plan is to stay first as long as I can. How long is that going to be? I have no idea. My focus is going to be on my driving and making no mistakes and making the best out of what I have.” Perhaps that will be enough for another checkmate.

Antonelli acknowledged that his engine-parts grid penalty meant he had no reason not to assist his teamate Russell by offering towing assistance.

He seemed a little peeved at times on the radio, but he did his job. With Russell likely to need to return the favour for him later this season, there is no point causing bother.

He told Sky Sports: “It’s what I have to do. The team asked me and of course I did what I had to do, I tried to help as much as possible. It’s a bit weird going in two, even the lap I did alone was a bit of a weird feeling. Overall with the penalty today I had to be a good teammate and I had to help as much as I could. I think I did a good job with that and happy it worked out.”

Here’s Oscar Piastri, asked if a pole had been possible: “I don’t think so, no. I think the first lap felt good and I tried to see if anyone wanted to go in front out of the pit lane but no one did and I knew it was always going to be difficult and misjudged the braking a little bit and locked up. That was the session but good to have a decent result, it has been a while. I’ll take it.”

Alpine managing director Steve Nielsen said to Sky Sports that they were aiming high: “Pierre is a class act, as you say, if you give him the machine, he will deliver. We failed to do that a few times last year. We haven’t always given him the most competitive machinery this year, but when we have he has delivered. Particularly earlier in the season so to see the team bounce back, to see him deliver on the track he knows well, he lives locally, he lives in Milan. It was wonderful.

“We mustn’t forget Franco either, he’s done a great job today. I really feel we have given them a good car, and who knows? Anything is possible tomorrow.”

Here’s what he said immediately after the session: “Massive congrats to Pierre because that’s an incredible performance. We were actually playing a game of chess about 15 minutes before qualifying and he beat me there and I thought ‘well I think I’ll beat you in qualifying’ and here we are - he’s ahead of me again! I was disappointed not to get pole. It was a bit messy with Verstappen opening the lap. But Pierre and Alpine have been super fast, even from Q1. Happy to see them get a good result.”

Gasly’s advantage, it appears, seems to be over Russell’s car understeering and lacking grip in turbulent air.

P1 ☝️#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/U0hebWsjWY

He says: “It was amazing, thank you everyone. It was an incredible qualy. I felt very good in the car. I was trying to chip away in evert session. I’m so happy, it’s been nine years trying to get a pole. First win [was] in Monza, to get pole is very special.”

He then pays credit to his team and the fans in Italian, and I am leaning on my Latin to get the gist of it.

“I was disappointed not to get the pole,” admits Russell who said he had been playing chess with Gasly before the game and the Frenchman won that, with Russell confident he was going to beat him in qualifying.

Alpine been in the news all weekend. Fair to say that pole lap from Gasly is better PR for the team than Flavio Briatore’s bizarre outburst in the FIA press conference yesterday. Well done that man.

His tone is evidently disappointed. In truth, given Hamilton is fifth, he is in a strong position to have the best of the weekend.

Gasly, yes, was fastest, but Russell has been the most consistent.

Piastri could be in trouble, too, for impeding earlier in the day’s sesion. Ferrari, in fourth and fifth, do not look entirely competitive.

Russell is second, Piastri third, Leclerc fourth, Hamilton fifth, Verstappen sixth, Antonelli seventh, Colapinto eighth, Norris ninth and Lindblad 10th.

He starts his flying lap, and locks up at turn 1 and exceeds track limits. That means Norris will be unable to get a tow from him too.

After being the quickest at FP2 and FP3, he is top of the pack once more with a bit over five minutes left.

Antonelli has done him a favour there, but Russell may need to return the favour in similar circumstances down the line.

Hamilton is now down in ninth, and struggling, about 0.8s off the pace.

Hamilton needs to catch Leclerc to get a tow. It failed to happen last time out.

Piastri finished Q2 in P2 but it looks likely he'll be penalised for this incident involving Lawson#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/RGzzEeqyql

Lawson, Hulkenberg, Sainz, Ocon, Bearman and Bortoleto are all out.

Hamilton is 10th, one-thousandth of a second quick enough to scrape through, and Leclrec ninth.

“**** me” exclaims Hamilton, without saying, ‘Asterisk’ once.

Antonelli asks for the chance to go out with another team ahead so he can get a tow of his own.

Norris now second quickest, so perhaps those brakes are up to speed.

There is some suggestion that Hamilton might need a front wing change.

The Silver Arrows working in tandem Kimi in front, George slipstreaming behind #F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/H476E91GJs

But Gasly is going fastest in his out lap.

Verstappen now goes fastest. Lawson is in behind, with Carlos Sainz making a surprise appearance up top.

Hamilton and Russell are yet to lay down times.

Norris is uncomfortable with his brakes at Monza.

Given he’s well outside of the fastest for now, the pressure is on him to make Q3.

The two Aston Martins are out, along with Yuki Tsunoda, Alex Albon, Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez.

Q2 awaits, with Gasly fastest - aiming for what would be his first pole.

Alonso, meanwhile, has wirthdrawn from the session. Things going wrong for the veteran, who must have no other hobbies.

FOUR MINUTES TO GO IN Q1TOP 6 ⬆️Gasly VerstappenColapintoAntonelliRussellHamiltonBOTTOM 6 ⬇️Hulkenberg AlbonBottasAlonsoStrollPerez#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BYdYjrjtnu

Pierre Gasly takes his Alpine for a spin. He is now fastest, with Verstappen second, and Colapinto bookending the Dutchman.

Antonelli and then Russell next, with the stricken Antonelli likely to give his colleague a tow.

The Red Bull man is 0.216s clear of Hamilton, with Piastri just behind.

No surprising stragglers just yet, but 11 minutes to go of this section.

We’ve 16 minutes left, and some cars are finally coming out to do battle.

18 minutes ahead before the final two rounds. Nobody is doing anything. As they say in football: tactically fascinating.

Monza paddock is absolutely sweltering. 33.8C out here. I just passed Fabio Capello on my way back to the media centre. He was speaking to Sky Sports Italia so I wasn’t able to give him my thoughts on where he went wrong at the 2010 World Cup.

Decent ding dong between Hamilton and Verstappen in practice earlier. Hopefully Hamilton is fired up for this. With Antonelli taking his grid drop at his home race, there’s a big opportunity for both Hamilton and Russell to close the gap this weekend.

The tifosi are ready 🙌It's time for qualifying at the Temple of Speed 👊#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/jeiTcb8Ij2

The cars will soon be out on the track, and we’ll have reports of their progress.

There are actually times when affection for a car company makes sense, despite what I said earlier.

Sound on... listen to the reception for Charles and Lewis ❤️#F1 #ItalianGP @ScuderiaFerrari pic.twitter.com/kk6BvA1UdC

As touched on earlier, Lewis Hamilton has to hope Charles Leclerc will work with him.

The Monegasque (look it up) is the junior partner at this point, whether he wants to be or not. That might not make him entirely delighted, but he can tow the British driver around and give him a launch for fast laps, if he’s feeling helpful.

Everyone now has access to PowerPoint, which means we all now have to have, “learnings.”

Imagine if someone you met in real life said that to you.

3 hours of laps and learnings done.#ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/GTvOvL5L5M

Given Antonelli is still one of the quickest on the track, it would be no surprise if he can at least make the top 10.

Favourable accidents and yellow flags might offer up more opportunities, too, but both Hamilton and Russell need to strike while they have such a clear advantage.

George Russell tops Lewis Hamilton in final practice in Monza 🇮🇹💪 pic.twitter.com/jxIO13aRX6

I’m as big a fan of F1 as the next man, assuming the next man quite likes F1, but there is something strange about supporting a car company, isn’t there?

🇮🇹 Sentendo il calore dell'Italia! 🥰🇬🇧 Feeling the warmth of Italy! 🥰 pic.twitter.com/ze6Ww1Z0zx

The session starts in around 40 minutes, so drivers are on their Gameboys and Instagram, and reading the weekend edition of The Telegraph.

Words we live by, this weekend and always ❤️ pic.twitter.com/0QoGlpzOHI

Here’s our interview with Alex Albon about a grim weekend at Monza.

“Alex Albon remembers the 2022 Italian Grand Prix well. He had been looking forward to it. ‘We had a car which was good down the straights that year so I was quite excited to be going to Monza,” the Williams driver recalls, a little wistfully.

‘We did FP1 and FP2 and sure enough we were quick so I was like: ‘This is going to be a good weekend.’

“Albon could not have been more wrong. He remembers waking at around 1am that night and being unable to get back to sleep.

“What happened next was the stuff of nightmares. Albon called the doctor, was diagnosed with appendicitis, sent to San Gerardo Hospital in Monza for surgery, only to suffer an unexpected complication during the procedure, which resulted in acute respiratory failure.”

He shares the joint record with Michael Schumacher for most wins at Monza.

Schumacher, a Ferrari legend, ended his career with five. Hamilton has the same.

Sport loves an emotional link to records, so be prepared for this to become a big moment.

Five wins apiece for Michael and Lewis 🖐#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/j10lMygYft

The Italian team are bringing an upgrade engine to Monza for the weekend.

Hamilton would desperately love to go out at the top after what is a remarkable return to decent form after some years of desperate struggle.

With Antonelli possibly out of the running this weekend, this is the chance to change the - *spits in self-scorn* - narrative.

Russell might have incurred a penalty if he had done this in qualifying.

The Mercedes man blocked Oscar Piastri’s run at a corner, forcing some heavy braking from his rival.

Thankfully, Piastri ducked out, and thankfully for Russell, he’s not facing censure.

A near miss for Oscar Piastri! 😬 pic.twitter.com/y6UMu8wIDM

Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton go racing! 🍿 pic.twitter.com/Zs8u8h4XoT

The former world champion is still looking for more from his car.

“Just looking at the deltas there, I was losing something like 0.6secs to George on the straights, which is something we need to look into,” Hamilton said yesterday, before explaining his conundrum for qualifying, suggesting he may go out after Leclerc.

“The tow is everything here so [I’m] likely to be looking for the tow.”

Because Antonelli exceeded the limit of parts used for his engine, he is taking a grid penalty at Monza.

Few would entirely rule out a storming ride for him on Sunday to end up top of the pack, but is is clearly a huge task for him to score points of any kind with that disadvantage.

They are now likely both past their peaks, but Hamilton and Verstappen recalled their battles of 2021 when they clashed in practice earlier.

Verstappen was already hacked off with Hamilton for seemingly obstructing his path earlier in the session, and they almost came together in the dying moments of the session.

Hamilton needed to take the escape road at the first chicane, where the pair made contact in 2021, as Verstappen looked to slip around his occasional rival. The two of them scarcely avoided another contact.

On the radios, Verstappen claimed, “He caused that,” while Hamilton reported to Ferrari that he was, “Blocked by Max.” Perhaps there will be more aggro later.

The full list of times from earlier today.

FP3 CLASSIFICATIONRussell in the box seat heading into qualifying#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BUrCsv92dT

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

Mattia Liberali has looked back on his decision to leave AC Milan and to snub rejoining them, insisting he has ‘no regrets’.

#1753. Stockport County vs Reading - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matthew Cooper | 12 Nov 2026 11:54, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 11:56

Stockport County will be looking to pick up an important victory when they welcome Reading to Edgeley Park on Saturday afternoon.

The hosts currently sit second in the League One table, while the visitors are sixth.

Stockport have collected 26 points from 14 league matches so far and sit just three points behind leaders Huddersfield Town.

Jimmy McNulty's side showed real resilience in the FA Cup at the weekend, coming from two goals down to beat Cray Wanderers 3-2 in extra time after goalkeeper Luca Ashby-Hammond was sent off.

In their most recent league game, Stockport beat Wimbledon thanks to goals from Jack Diamond and Ethan Ennis.

It was a crucial victory for the Hatters, who had dropped points in their previous two games with a 1-1 draw against Notts County and a 1-0 defeat to Oxford United.

It is also worth noting that Stockport failed to beat Reading at all last season, drawing 1-1 at home before losing 1-0 at the Select Car Leasing Stadium.

Reading sit sixth with 22 points from 14 matches, leaving them just four points behind Stockport and firmly in the race for promotion.

The Royals were beaten 2-0 by rivals Oxford United in their last league game, but responded with an emphatic 5-0 FA Cup victory over Peterborough United three days later.

Daniel Kyerewaa, Jack Marriott and Charlie Savage all found the back of the net in the first half, while Jamie Reid came off the bench to bag a brace.

Reading will be looking to carry that momentum into Saturday's fixture, having rested almost all of their first team players on Tuesday when they lost on penalties to Bristol Rovers in the EFL Trophy.

Stockport County form (all competitions):

Stockport have been handed a boost after goalkeeper Oliver Whatmuff withdrew from the England Under-20 squad to remain with the club following Ashby-Hammond's dismissal against Cray Wanderers.

As a result, Stockport are expected to pick the same side that beat Wimbledon, with Kyle Wootton leading the line and Diamond and Benony Breki Andresson featuring out wide.

Reading, meanwhile, are set to be without Paudie O'Connor and Andy Rinomhota through suspension after the pair picked up their fifth yellow cards of the campaign against Oxford.

Paddy Lane, Benn Ward and George Earthy remain sidelined through injury, but Reading will be hopeful Udoka Godwin-Malife is fit after he picked up a knock against Peterborough.

Josh Knight and Liam Fraser are expected to replace O'Connor and Rinomhota, while Savage could get the nod over Josh Stokes in the No.10 role.

Stockport County possible starting lineup:

Whatmuff; Pye, Jobe, O'Connell; Dacres-Cogley, Norwood, Fiorini, Ennis; Diamond, Wootton, Andresson

Pereira; Godwin-Malife, Knight, Dorsett, Roberts; Knight, Wing; Lisbie, Savage, Kyerewaa; Marriott

Stockport have a very strong home record, having won five of their seven league games so far this season, and they should have enough to beat a Reading side that is missing several key players.

#1752. Man United are a rotten, shambolic mess. They lack intelligence, look uncoached and fumbling, failing Michael Carrick is not the man to arrest this trauma, writes IAN LADYMAN

Published: 14:32 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 20:25 EST, 8 November 2026

Manchester United do not have a football team, more a collection of adrenaline junkies. Over time, it will not be enough.

So deficient are Michael Carrick's players that they surely can't keep their manager in a job for much longer. For the most part United are shambolic, a mess. At times they play football so devoid of intelligence and competence that it's almost impossible to fathom. They look uncoached.

Yet here they were for the second night running at Old Trafford, completing a lap of honour at full-time while their supporters sang the name of Carrick as he completed his own journey in front of the Stretford End towards the tunnel.

United – it's worth pointing out – are third bottom of the Premier League. They haven't won in the league since August and have conceded more goals across all competitions – 30 – than any team bar Crystal Palace in Europe's top divisions.

But at Old Trafford they will cling to anything to help them look in the mirror without laughing and currently the currency is comebacks. There was one against Roma in the Champions League last Tuesday and here – quite remarkably – there were two in one game.

None of it should really mean anything in the grand scheme. United are rotten, capable of playing effectively only when something gives them an energy spike with which to roll. It makes for quite hypnotic theatre but has inadequacy and desperation at its core.

Patrick Dorgu (centre) scored a late equaliser as troubled Man United drew 4-4 vs Aston Villa

Dorgu scored in the 96th-minute with this header but United sit 18th in the Premier League

Despite the draw, Michael Carrick's position as United head coach looks increasingly doubtful

It won't sustain them or indeed their fumbling, failing manager. But for the moment it's what they have and what they are.

MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1): Lammens 4; Mazraoui 4, Yoro 6, Maguire 5 (Heaven 46, 5), Dalot 3 (Dorgu 66, 8); Tielemans 6 (Mount 66, 5), Mainoo 6; Amad 5 (Lacey 66, 7), Fernandes 6, Cunha 7; Mbeumo 5 (Zirkzee 83, 7)

Goals: Fernandes (16 pen), Tielemans (44), Zirkzee (90+2), Dorgu (90+6)

ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Harwood-Bellis 5, Lindelof 6, Torres 6, Maatsen 4; Goretzka 6 (Mbaye 78, 6), Kamara 4; Alysson 7 (Barkley 71, 6), McGinn 8 (Hemmings 71, 6), Manzambi 6; Jackson 6 (Madjo 86)

Goals: Alysson (1), Jackson (4), McGinn (48 pen), Goretzka (53)

Here, they twice trailed by two, at the start of both halves. They were 2-0 down after only four minutes and 4-2 behind after 53. Somehow they managed not to lose.

The two goals United scored in added time at the end of the game came from absolutely nowhere. On the touchline Carrick – free from total humiliation for the second time in six days – raised a single finger to the sky.

In the directors' box – where the TV companies seem to have a camera permanently trained these days – fist pumps were in evidence from those in United blazers.

This was another uncomfortable afternoon for Messrs Ratcliffe, Wilcox and Berrada. A collection of new banners in the crowd made feelings known.

For now, Carrick is being spared any of the blame. That is strange and wrong but tells us much about the confused nature of the modern United. If they blame one of their own then they really do have nowhere left to go in search of self-respect.

United's opening against Roma last week had been traumatic enough. This was even worse but the root of it was desperately familiar – incompetent football.

The hapless United full-back Diogo Dalot was to blame for the first goal as Villa's Brazilian Alysson blasted his shot through the Portuguese's limp challenge. Later – after conceding a second half penalty – Dalot was booed off by his own fans.

That was painful and unedifying but completely understandable. Dalot has played more than 250 games for United yet has never even been good enough.

Aston Villa took the lead after just 59 seconds when Alysson (centre) scored at Old Trafford

Nicolas Jackson (centre) doubled the visitors' lead on four minutes as they made a dream start

Bruno Fernandes pulled one back for the hosts with a penalty on 16 minutes in a crazy start

For goal two, goalkeeper Senne Lammens was culpable as he pushed Alysson's shot into the path of Nicolas Jackson.

Once again United were in sink or swim territory. Once again, amazingly, they kept their heads above water – at least for a while.

Boubacar Kamara's 13th minute challenge on Matheus Cunha was stupid as the Brazilian was heading away from goal. But the Bruno Fernandes penalty that followed was calm and precise and the shot of belief United needed was theirs.

For the next 20 minutes or so, Carrick's team played well off the back of it. It was the only part of their game that will look good on the highlights. The United front four pressed and harried the Villa defence to the extent that Unai Emery's team couldn't get up the field.

Villa keeper Zion Suzuki saved well from a Cunha curler while subsequent shots from Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo and Amad Diallo took deflections and narrowly missed the target.

At some stage it felt as though United's energy must drop. Over time it did. But then they equalised.

Moments after seeing Suzuki save one of his own efforts, Amad found space to pull the ball back for Youri Tielemans who placed his first United goal in from 18 yards against his old club. Carrick's team deserved to be level at that stage and had played some enterprising football to get there. But their self-harm gene surfaced again before long.

Youri Tielemans (right) brought United level before half-time with this strike vs his old club

John McGinn put Villa ahead again just minutes after half-time from the penalty spot

Leon Goretkza (left) made it 4-2 to Villa with this close-range strike as they looked set to win

Joshua Zirkzee (left) pulled one back in second-half stoppage-time with this finish for United

Alysson had almost scored with the last big moment of the first half and in the 47th minute he drew an utterly dumb foul from Dalot and John McGinn scored the penalty firmly.

United are beyond compare in the Premier League when it comes to this kind of thing. Who else in the top flight concedes the kind of goals they do? A case in point came in the 53rd minute.

McGinn's free-kick was heading across goal and away when United defender Leny Yoro inexplicably headed it towards his own goal. Lammens somehow touched the ball on to the bar but when it dropped Leon Goretzka poked it in.

That was the 16th goal United had conceded in the last five games and this time the attempt at a fightback was more muted.

There were some half chances – shots from Cunha and Fernandes – and some territory in which to play.

But this was a game Villa were now able to control rather better and they looked set to ease home until Patrick Dorgu crossed for Joshua Zirkzee to ease a goal in from out of nothing in the 2nd minute of added time.

Old Trafford was emptying fast by the time Dorgu headed in a 96th equaliser from a corner. But by then the collective blood was up once more and it was enough.

Villa appealed for a foul on goalkeeper Suzuki and it's true Lammens had gone looking for him. Was the contact between the two 'keepers significant enough to warrant VAR intervention? Probably not. United had their draw and they had a point.

If the season ended today, they would be down. Yet they were cheered off. Some things you just can't make up.

#1751. ‘Not ready’, ‘out of control’ and ‘the end of the world’: What Amorim’s words tell us about Milan’s state

Ruben Amorim is not one to hold back when it comes to speaking his thoughts to the media, and the last few days are no exception.

The past week or so has seen Amorim have to digest the best and worst of his AC Milan side. The 3-1 derby win over Inter generated a euphoria that begun whispers of the word ‘Scudetto’, before a dismal defeat to Ferencvaros which saw Milan drop to 29th in the Europa League standings.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This rollercoaster of extremes didn’t stop either side of those two games either. Before the victory over the Nerazzurri a 2-1 lead had been coughed up against Bologna, who scored three times in the second half to win at San Siro and inflict the first league defeat on the Rossoneri.

Yesterday, the Diavolo responded to the season low-point against the Hungarians by beating a Genoa side that had won their last three games and four of their last five. This Milan team is a very difficult one to work out, and it seems even the manager is struggling to do so.

After the Ferencvaros and Genoa games, we learned a lot about where Amorim sees his team to be at. Some key lines from his post-match comments demonstrated a wide spectrum of reaction, from anger to pride, passing through encouragement and worry.

Ruben Amorim has often gone to bat for his players after negative performances and results this season, but it seems that the defeat on Thursday night had pushed his patience to the brink as he tore into his team after the game.

“There’s no explanation. There’s nothing I can say, especially about the first half. I don’t remember another first half like it. It’s about ambition, concentration, desire,” he said.

“We gave away opportunities, we gave away stupid gifts. We weren’t prepared to play football tonight. I usually have a lot to say in defence of our team, but not tonight. We need to be more humble and understand what happened.”

For the first time we saw a peek behind the mask, one that has very often been one portraying an optimistic and positive expression. Amorim knew there was no point attempting to lie to the supporters, the media but above all to himself.

What we know is that Amorim echoed the ferocity of these sentiments when speaking in the dressing room after full-time in what was likely the first dressing down that the team got. Six players were reported to have disappointed more than the others, too.

Above all, what stood out was the fact that the head coach opted to question whether his players wanted it enough. This was no longer a question of learning an identity, rotation or an injury crisis: it became a matter of heart.

Another intriguing extract from the post-Ferencvaros tirade that Amorim went on was about the squad’s ability to balance playing in two different competitions, namely Serie A and the Europa League.

“We’re not ready to be competitive on two fronts. We need to work on our way of looking at football and how we approach matches. There are no excuses tonight, there’s nothing I can say.

“I have to focus on the league, obviously, but we also have to do well in the Europa League. We must and can win games despite the rotation. We have to be ready – we’re not now – to play and win every three days.

“But I won’t give up on this competition. But as long as the mathematics don’t condemn us, we’ll fight in this competition as we do in the others.”

Once again, Amorim offered a bit of a revelation: the league is the absolute priority for Milan this season. It may not exactly be revolutionary information, given that a top four spot remains the most accessible avenue to the main objective for 2026-27: securing a Champions League return.

And yet, in his emotional outburst, the former Sporting CP and Manchester United boss told us all in black and white that Serie A will be the focus. As a result, it’s right to expect more ups and downs in Europe, especially with such a depleted squad.

There is an element of observational realism about Amorim’s words; almost an admission of defeat in his attempts to spin two plates at the same time and get the most out of the resources at his disposal. Does it suggest a Europa League resurgence is coming? Not exactly.

Amorim has not made a habit of mentioning individuals ever since his arrivals, both in his pre-match words but especially after games in which emotions are running high. However, he brought up someone who was absent for the Ferencvaros game.

“Everyone needs to train like Pavlovic. He’s ready to die in training. He’s a good example. Sometimes when players don’t start, they struggle. But there are no excuses, we should have won even with those who started,” he said.

Going into the season there were some who were legitimately questioning whether Strahinja Pavlovic would even be a tactical fit for Amorim’s usual 3-4-2-1 system, given that he prefers more composed, ball-playing outside centre-backs.

The answer to those doubts is that in November the Serbian has become the shining light in the eyes of his manager. We mentioned earlier that it had become a question of heart, and nobody can doubt that Pavlovic has that in abundance.

For all of the talk about tactics, systems, shapes and patterns, football is a simple game that very often comes down to who wants it more. In this regard, Amorim elevated Pavlovic as the example to follow, while hoping he returns from injury for the Frosinone game after the break.

Moving on to the post-Genoa reflections, what was quite apparent was that Ruben Amorim was in no mood to get carried away. In fact, if anything, he revealed his belief that his team are still miles off where he wants them.

“What I feel is that, when we’re competitive, we’re difficult to beat, and now we’re steering the game towards our style. We push for control with the ball.

“When we’re not able to be competitive, we’re completely out of control. It’s a big difference, but it’s something we need to work on. But again, the team’s evolution, the way we’re playing, is completely different from the start of the season, and I’m happy with that.

“We should have more points. I’m clearly not happy with the European games, not just because of the results, but because of the performance. Results can happen, but the performances are far from what we want. However, I think we’ll be a better team in the future.”

So, for now this version of Milan is not one that satisfies the coach. The words are a good summary of what the last six games have shown, in which there have been an even split of victories and defeats: on their day the team can beat anyone in the league, but on an off-day they can lose to anyone too.

What Amorim seems keen to hammer home is that progress for this season will be judged on the ability to bring the ceiling closer to the floor. In other words, we have seen the potential of this team already with some impressive wins, yet the base level for performances remains frighteningly low.

Consistency is not just about being able to string together several positive results in a row, something the current Rossoneri do not seem capable of. It is about the repeated displaying of an idea and an identity every few days, to suggest the team are getting closer to the vision the coach has.

Various things make that difficult (perhaps unachievable, based on Amorim’s other comments) right now, such as the injury situation and the multiple windows needed to sculpt the squad. Progress is not always linear, but the target has been set.

One of the themes that Amorim has been consistently questioned on this season is how to unlock the club-record signing Goncalo Ramos, who remains stuck on three goals (one of which was a penalty).

After the Genoa game, he said: “I think we’re lacking time in the final third. We control the ball away from the opponent’s penalty area. This is also key for Goncalo Ramos to have more clear-cut chances. It’s clearly not Goncalo’s fault.

“Pulisic is far from the penalty area. Gonçalo is far from the penalty area. All these players play away from the penalty area, so I can say we’re still far from the final product, because we’re still working on good progression, but then in the final third of the pitch we waste a lot of time with the ball there.”

This is one of the points of ‘evolution’ that Amorim clearly wants to see from his side, but is yet to achieve. Milan are not yet a team that can sustain pressure in the opposition half, nor can they penetrate the box with any regularity either.

In fact, a report from Sky backed this up with some interesting numbers, look specifically at data per 30 minutes of actual possession. Milan are first in Serie A for build-up actions, but they are 20th for entries into the final third and entries into the opposition box.

Amorim’s side are 19th for percentage of touches in the attacking third and 18th in percentage of touches in the opposition box. When the Rossoneri have the ball, it is rarely in a threatening area.

With numbers like these, there isn’t much for Ramos to get on the end of, and it makes the positive attacking numbers (23 goals in 11 league games) feel quite unsustainable.

The Portuguese striker meanwhile is first in the Milan squad in Serie A for interceptions, recoveries, touches in the middle third and touches in the opposition half. He is second for receptions, touches and duels, and third for passes.

Simply put, the No.9 is being drawn away from the area he should be operating in because the team are not capable of sustaining spells of possession further up the field, so he needs to drop deeper to feel involved.

This is something Amorim must work on, because while the goals are coming from other sources for now – in some cases due to the space Ramos helps create – it could all come tumbling down unless the attacking play improves more generally.

🚨🎙️🛡️ Ruben Amorim on Gonçalo Ramos: “Ramos is helping US more than we are helping him. It’s a TEAM problem, not a Ramos problem.”

“We don’t spend enough time in the final third.”

“When we start keeping the ball there more often, Gonçalo is going to score MANY goals.” pic.twitter.com/b3Zs6YxNym

— Milan Wire (@MilanWireX) November 8, 2026

Finally, we end with what was perhaps the most passionate part of Amorim’s comments following the win at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris on Sunday, again centred around the levels he expects from his team.

“It’s the mentality. When you’re a player, there are no off days. If you play for Milan, for these clubs, there are no off days. You can’t show up like we did on Thursday and then turn it on again for Sunday. It’s not possible, it’s not something that will work.

“It’s not a physical condition, it’s a question of anxiety about defeat. If you ‘panic’ about defeat, it’s not that you’re afraid of losing, but that you know that losing is the end of the world. That’s the feeling I want my teams to have.”

In many ways, the manager was speaking in a way that channels how fans have experienced the past week. How is it possible that Milan can be completely outplayed by a side sat third in the Hungarian lead just days after convincingly beating the Italian champions?

Against Genoa, how can the team play as they did in the first half, and then appear to completely drop off a cliff in the second half when the time came to dig deep and bring the result home? The disparity in levels both in-game and from match to match is astounding everyone, even the man in charge.

What Amorim said about wanting his side to fear losing was particularly poignant. In his time at the club so far he has repeatedly stressed that feeling of responsibility to honour the red and black shirt and all that comes with that, including the importance of results.

Some may argue that encouraging an ‘end of the world’ type mentality will not help the players play more carefree and will actually only stiffen them up. Yet, it could also provide the stimulus for the fight and the courage that Amorim clearly so desperately wants.

There is a hint of irony about the ‘no days off’ comment, as Amorim has given the squad a one-week break, at least those who were not called up by their national teams. When everyone reconvenes there will be another crucial stretch of games to see out the year, starting with a home match against the surprise package Frosinone.

For all of the energy, passion and emotion that Ruben Amorim speaks with, it will eventually be time for words to become deeds. Consistency must be not a distant mirage but some thing tangible that emerges.

Only then will a full buy-in be achieved and patience be awarded. Otherwise there will always be the fear that darkness follows light.

#1750. Michael Carrick, Man Utd break unwanted all-time records after sacking confirmed with club statement

By Oliver Thomas | 12 Nov 2026 12:17

Michael Carrick has officially been sacked as Manchester United head coach and has departed Old Trafford with an unwanted all-time record.

The 45-year-old’s inevitable exit was confirmed on Thursday morning with a club statement explaining why the “extremely difficult” decision was made.

“Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025-26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period.

“After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

“Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.

“The club intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible.”

Four months after becoming Man United’s interim boss following the dismissal of Ruben Amorim, Carrick was rewarded with the permanent role in May after steering the club back into the Champions League.

However, Carrick has now left Man United sitting in 18th place in the Premier League table following the club’s worst start to a season for 40 years, accumulating only eight points from their opening 10 games (W1 D5 L4).

Although Red Devils supporters have continued to give their full backing to Carrick, acknowledging that deeper issues lie with the club's hierarchy, the decision has been made for the club to move in a new direction.

Carrick has therefore set an unwanted record of overseeing the fewest games as a permanent Man United manager (32 in total, 16 as permanent boss), overtaking Clarence "Lal" Hilditch (33) who was in charge between October 1926 and April 1927.

Across those 32 games, Carrick won 15, drew eight and lost nine in all competitions (46.9% win rate), though he only recorded four victories across his final 16 matches in charge (25% win rate).

Meanwhile, Man United have now sacked two managers (Carrick in November and Amorim in January) in the same calendar year for the first time in their 148-year history.

Carrick’s exit also means that the Red Devils have sacked managers in three successive seasons for the very first time.

Prior to the dismissals of Carrick and Amorim, Erik ten Hag was relieved of his duties in October 2024, just four months after being given a new contract.

Man United have had a total of seven permanent managers and five different interim bosses since club icon Sir Alex Ferguson called time on his legendary 26-year reign in the summer of 2013.

It is widely expected that Mauricio Pochettino will be appointed as Carrick’s successor, with an agreement in principle said to be in place for him to swap his current role as USA national team coach for the Old Trafford hotseat.

#1749. Kosovo vs Israel - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 12 Nov 2026 12:34

Kosovo and Israel will clash at Stadiumi Fadil Vokrri on Saturday afternoon in UEFA Nations League B Group 3.

The hosts are second in the standings with five points from four games, while the visitors are at the bottom of the table with two points after four matches.

Kosovo got their 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign underway with a deserved 1-0 victory over Ireland, with captain Vedat Muriqi scoring the late winner.

Franco Foda's side had dominated the encounter, holding 57% possession, taking 22 shots and creating 2.74 expected goals (xG) compared to Ireland's three efforts and 0.25xG.

Foda would have been looking for his team to build on that triumph in the following matches, but Kosovo have failed to win any of the subsequent three fixtures.

Kosovo suffered a 3-1 defeat to Austria on matchday two, followed by back-to-back draws with Israel (0-0) and Austria (1-1), leaving them second in the standings with five points, only ahead of third-placed Ireland thanks to their head-to-head record.

Ahead of a potentially pivotal matchday six encounter with Ireland, when both teams could be fighting to secure second place and a chance at promotion to League A, Kosovo will be eager to secure all three points on Saturday - especially as Ireland face leaders Austria.

Kosovo, despite failing to score, were in control of large periods of their 0-0 draw with Israel, and a return to their home ground for the reverse fixture will provide a considerable confidence boost.

Isreal also head into this encounter having failed to win any of their four League B Group 3 fixtures, suffering two defeats and recording two draws.

Ran Ben Simon's side, as a result, sit fourth in the standings with two points, trailing the third and fourth-placed sides by three points with two games remaining.

Israel will, therefore, have to secure a victory on Saturday and hope for results to go their way on the final day if they are to avoid having to compete in the relegation playoff fixture.

Israel will draw confidence from each of their two goals scored in League B Group 3 having come away from home, although they have conceded four goals in those two away games.

Israel have, however, failed to beat Kosovo in any of their three clashes, suffering one defeat and recording two draws, conceding twice and scoring only once in those matches.

Captain Muriqi and Edon Zhegrova have scored two of Kosovo's three goals, and both are expected to start alongside Baton Zabergja in attack on Saturday.

Meanwhile, Israel are likely to start Oscar Gloukh and Liel Abada behind Dor Turgeman in attack, while captain Dor Peretz should start in the centre of a midfield three.

Further back, Roy Revivo and Ilay Feingold will provide width from full-back, with Nikita Stoinov and Eli Dasa in central defence.

#1748. Mauricio Pochettino should not take Man Utd job - unless two 'needed' signings are made

By Oliver Thomas | 12 Nov 2026 12:38

Gary Neville has warned Mauricio Pochettino against becoming the next Manchester United head coach unless he is promised two new signings in January.

It was confirmed on Thursday morning that Michael Carrick has been relieved of his duties just six months after his permanent appointment, with the Red Devils revealing in a statement that they “intend to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible.”

The man expected to replace Carrick is former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea boss Pochettino, who reportedly has an agreement in principle to swap his current role in charge of the USA national team with the Old Trafford hotseat.

Pochettino, 54, is set to take over a Man United side languishing inside the Premier League relegation zone following the club’s worst start to a season in 40 years.

The struggling Red Devils have looked particularly vulnerable in defence, conceding 19 goals across their opening 10 league games – only Ipswich Town (20) and basement club Crystal Palace (24) having conceded more.

Ahead of Pochettino’s expected arrival, former Man United defender Neville believes that the Argentine should be assured by the club’s hierarchy that he can make at least two defensive signings in January before accepting the manager’s job.

Speaking on The Overlap, Neville said: “If I was Mauricio Pochettino now, I would be literally protecting myself up to the high heaven.

“He'll do that with a pay-off, so do that in your contract, but secondly, he needs two defenders in January, so he's got to insist that he gets two defenders in January.

“He's got to insist that he gets a minimum budget next summer for the transfer window to be able to turn this around. He's got to insist that he gets a budget that follows.

“They have to give it to him or else he shouldn't take the job.”

Neville added: “He's got to insist on the way in that there's some sort of transfer control, some form of budget there that he knows he can meaningfully change the team.

“Mauricio, I don't think is the kind of manager either who would say 'Give me half a billion' - I don't think he's that type of guy, I think he's someone who is a bit more responsible and will look at things.

"He'll want to bring players through and he'll want to develop young players - I get that and he'll do that. I just think he needs to protect himself in these next 12 months with the transfer budget. He has to.

“The only time you can insist upon it is at the very beginning and he needs two defenders in January.”

Neville, who made 602 appearances for Man United and is regarded as one of England’s greatest right-backs, did not hold back on his criticism of the Red Devils’ current defensive options.

“I mean look at the back four that he finished with on Sunday (4-4 draw with Aston Villa). It was [Diogo] Dalot left-back, [Noussair] Mazraoui right-back, Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven,” Neville added.

“That is probably the worst back four in the Premier League. I don't know a back four that is worse than that in the Premier League right now if I watch it. I can't believe Manchester United have ended up with that back four.”

Man United have been linked with a plethora of defenders throughout this calendar year, but their top left-back target Lewis Hall signed a long-term contract extension at Newcastle in September, seemingly ending their pursuit of the Englishman.

Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde, Manchester City’s Rayan Ait-Nouri, RB Leipzig’s David Raum and Rennes starlet Mahamadou Nagida are among a number of other left-backs who have been linked with Man United.

The likes of Roma’s Wesley, Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite, Fulham’s Calvin Bassey, Brentford’s Nathan Collins and Nottingham Forest’s Murillo are other defenders who are believed to be on the Red Devils’ radar ahead of the winter window.

Pochettino could be announced as Man United’s new manager before the club travels to Anfield for their next Premier League match against Liverpool on November 22.

#1746. GdS: Milan ready €50m January assault for Tresoldi to give Ramos a partner – the strategy

AC Milan are serious about signing Nicolo Tresoldi from Club Brugge, with an attempt being readied ahead of the winter window.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, Milan intend to sign another striker even before the summer arrives, in order to boost their Champions League hopes. The name that they have chosen is someone the fans already know well: Nicolo Tresoldi.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

At the end of June, the club announced the signing of Gonçalo Ramos for over €70m, the most expensive signing in the club’s history to date (and likely for a while to come). Ramos hasn’t – at least for now – cured Milan’s goal-scoring deficiency in the No.9 role.

The negotiations for Tresoldi, however, are shaping up to be costly. Last summer, Club Brugge rejected another Italian offer of €35m from Roma, and in the meantime the price has skyrocketed after the forward bagged 13 goals in 15 games.

Adding his four goals this season against Germany’s youth team brings him close to 20 for the season already. His league hat-trick against VV Sint-Truiden at the end of October followed his hat-trick at San Siro against Inter, marking the night that every Rossoneri fan knew his name.

Therefore, the cost could now be around €50m, another huge expense if Milan really decide to go all-in. The club made a €24m loss in the last accounts after three years of profit, and the temptation is to speculate to accumulate, i.e. to invest more and make sure of the Champions League revenues.

There’s a desire to finalise the deal as early as the January transfer window, unless Brugge move to raise the price, perhaps due to a potential foreign competition. Milan believe that their relationship with the Belgian side is actually strong, with Gerry Cardinale ready to lead talks again.

As for Ramos, the investment so far has yielded just three goals and two assists, which doesn’t mean he wasn’t effective and is ready to be shelved, but it’s precisely when paired with another striker that the management believes the Portuguese could be more productive.

In short, a two-striker team can’t be ruled out in the future, with Tresoldi alongside the former Benfica man. In the European race goals fuel the climb, and Milan know this after last season’s late collapse, keen to avoid it again.

Should Milan hit a wall erected by Club Brugge, they would leave the Tresoldi option open for the summer. In the meantime, they would fill the gap with a striker on loan from a top European club.

However, Tresoldi could provide an initial assist for Milan: his support for the Rossoneri is well-known and has been publicly stated, so among the various options available, Nicolò would choose the San Siro.

A permanent return to Italy could also benefit coach Roberto Mancini, who – after the Under-21 European Championship (which Tresoldi will compete in with Germany) – would finally like him to play for the senior Azzurri side.

Nicolò, born in Cagliari in August 2004, is still free to choose which (senior) national team he wants to represent, and Mancini expressed his confidence earlier this week: “I spoke to Tresoldi, and Ranieri spoke to us too. First of all, I think he needs to feel the desire to play for Italy.

“He was born in Italy, like his father [former defender Emanuele], who played for the Under-21s and won the European Championship. I think there’s a chance he’ll choose the Azzurri. He knows he can be an important player for our future, and I hope he makes the right choice.”

Even in such an extreme scenario, seeing how Mamadou Sakho and Kolo Toure may possibly return within the week, these signings make no sense. You donai??i??t spend A?7 to A?10 million on players just to feature in a few games. Hopefully Liverpool FC will make it out of this window without any such expenditures.

History teaches us that short-cuts and quick-fixes can be accompanied by pretty massive pitfalls. Liverpool FC fans need to stop looking to the transfer market for the answers. Jurgen Klopp is at the helm, and his methods require investing time and effort in the players he works with. Heai??i??ll sign players when he comes across the right ones, but hopefully wonai??i??t be spending money searching for some unicorn signing that will miraculously fly the club to success.

And it is absolutely the right approach to take.

#1744. Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

Newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

Even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4

For the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

“It shows where we have potential,” he said. “There are elements to improve offensively.

“The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads showed big character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”

A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another new signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

Justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

That is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

Speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss said: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

“We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads showed the right reaction.”

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx

Oh dear not a great moment for two of Newcastle’s summer signings as Bournemouth extend their lead. Amar Dedic lost the ball with a heavy touch and Nico Gonzalez’s half hearted tackle failed to halt Bournenouth’s counter attack.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under new head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

Despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. New signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

At opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.
